value.text: Our strategy is to deliver insights and experiences essential to investing, with a keen focus on innovation across data, research, product, and delivery

strategic_priorities.quote: Our strategy is to deliver insights and experiences essential to investing. Proprietary data sets, meaningful analytics, independent research, and effective investment strategies are at the core of the powerful digital solutions that investors across our client segments rely on. We have a keen focus on innovation across data, research, product, and delivery so that we can effectively cater to the evolving needs and expectations of investors globally.

value.text: Deliver differentiated insights across asset classes to public and private market investors

strategic_priorities.quote:
Deliver differentiated insights across asset classes to public and private market investors
Shifting investor needs and expectations, innovative investment approaches and technologies, and a changing political and regulatory environment continue to drive the evolution of the financial services industry. We remain committed to ensuring that the modern investor is empowered with new data, research, and analytics.

value.text: Establish a leading ESG position across each business

strategic_priorities.quote:
Establish a leading ESG position across each business
The Sustainalytics acquisition in 2020 has positioned us to successfully drive ESG across the investing landscape, which is a pivotal part of our long-term strategy. We remain focused on the growth of Sustainalytics and its ESG ratings, while prioritizing ESG integration across all areas of our business

value.text: Drive operational excellence and scalability to support growth targets

strategic_priorities.quote:
Drive operational excellence and scalability to support growth targets
We have grown significantly in the last few years, and as we have continued to focus on growth in 2021 and beyond, we are emphasizing execution and scalability in our operations, processes, and technology.

value.text: Build an inclusive culture that drives exceptional talent engagement and development

strategic_priorities.quote:
Build an inclusive culture that drives exceptional talent engagement and development
Morningstar is committed to investing in talent and building a culture that realizes our DEI goals.

value.text: Expand investment and credit research capabilities and enhance existing products and services (research and development)

strategic_priorities.quote: A key aspect of our growth strategy is to expand our investment and credit research capabilities and enhance our existing products and services.

value.text: Build a comprehensive Wealth Management platform leveraging capabilities from Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts, and Morningstar.com, including launching direct indexing through the TAMP

strategic_priorities.quote: We plan to launch direct indexing capabilities through the TAMP later in 2022, as part of our recently-announced strategy to build a comprehensive Wealth Management platform leveraging capabilities from Morningstar Office, ByAllAccounts, and Morningstar.com.

value.text: Expand wealth management platform capabilities internationally via the agreed acquisition of Praemium's U.K. and international business

strategic_priorities.quote: In 2021, Morningstar agreed to acquire Praemium’s U.K. and international wealth management platform business. Praemium offers proprietary, friction-free, SaaS-based technology and services that allow fee-based advisors to outsource key elements of the advice workflow. The platform will enable us to expand our wealth management platform capabilities internationally beyond the U.S. and India.

value.text: Longer term, MCIA plans to offer modular credit information products that leverage our credit expertise and embed in customer workflows

strategic_priorities.quote: Longer term, MCIA plans to offer modular credit information products that leverage our credit expertise and embed in the workflows of internal and external customers.

value.description: Advisory vote approving Morningstar's executive compensation.

events.quote: Morningstar’s executive compensation was approved, on an advisory basis, with the voting as follows:

value.why_notable: Recurring, unusually explicit statement of Morningstar's no-guidance philosophy, framing management incentives directly.

notable_language.quote: We do not make public financial forecasts for our business because we want to avoid creating any incentives for our management team to make speculative statements about our financial results that could influence our stock price or take actions that help us meet short-term forecasts, but may not build long-term shareholder value.

value.why_notable: Direct admission of wage inflation and employee turnover pressure affecting the company, new emphasis relative to prior pandemic disclosure.

notable_language.quote: Certain long-term effects of the efforts of monetary authorities and governments to ameliorate the impacts of the pandemic are potentially starting to become evident, including both price and wage inflation as well as the competition for workers. We have noted these effects in our business related to the mobility of employees between jobs and the wage levels needed to hire or retain employees.

value.why_notable: Hedged COVID framing paired with an explicit claim of no significant revenue impact — a softening from earlier pandemic uncertainty language.

notable_language.quote: The threat of new variants of the virus and concerns over the adoption and efficacy of mitigants, such as vaccines and other treatments, continue to affect historical commercial and work patterns, although not with any significant impact on any of our sources of revenue during 2021.

value.why_notable: Acknowledges client losses in Investment Management, an admission embedded in otherwise positive growth commentary.

notable_language.quote: Investment Management revenue grew 6.1% in 2021, as stronger year-over-year inflows and market performance more than offset the negative impact of previously-disclosed client losses.

value.why_notable: Unusually direct admission that the company's own risk of inadvertent regulatory noncompliance has risen.

notable_language.quote: Given more intense regulatory scrutiny and the novelty of some of the issues presented, the possibilities for inadvertent noncompliance with regulation have increased.

value.why_notable: New-for-the-year topic; a plain statement of limited impact with a forward hedge on IT infrastructure.

notable_language.quote: Given the nature of our business, global supply chain disruptions have had little impact on the company, but could impact the availability of certain IT infrastructure over time.

value.why_notable: Explicit explanation of the reversal of the COVID-era weighting change back to the pre-pandemic mix, described as 'the optimal mix'.

notable_language.quote: We modified our annual incentive performance measure weightings for 2021 to 67% Adjusted Revenue and 33% Adjusted EBITDA. This represents the weighting which we believe is the optimal mix of performance measures for our annual incentive plan and is what we had in place in 2019. In 2020, we modified our weightings to 50% Adjusted Revenue and 50% Adjusted EBITDA in response to the COVID-19 pandemic and the uncertainty it caused.

value.why_notable: Justifies a doubling of upside leverage purely by reference to 'market practices'.

notable_language.quote: For our performance-based Market Stock Unit Program, starting with our November 2021 grant, we increased our maximum payout to 200% of target, which represents a change to align to market practices.

value.why_notable: Recurring philosophy statement reserving discretion while claiming formulaic alignment.

notable_language.quote: Does not use rigid formulas to determine executive compensation but nevertheless aims to tie annual cash incentive compensation closely to value creation, as measured by increases in Adjusted Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA or similar measures.

value.why_notable: Explains replacement of an objective revenue metric with a committee-determined discretionary kicker, still attributed to the pandemic in 2021.

notable_language.quote: The shift from a revenue kicker in 2019 to a performance kicker in 2020 and 2021 was made due to the uncertain market environment and uncertain three-year outlook due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

value.why_notable: Long-recurring rationale for the Executive Chairman's nominal pay, framed as his own request.

notable_language.quote: In consideration of his status as our principal shareholder, Joe believes that his compensation should be directly aligned with other shareholders and be realized primarily through appreciation in the long-term value of our common stock. At his request and supported by the Compensation Committee, he did not participate in our equity or cash-based incentive programs in 2021 and his salary has been $100,000 since 2000.

value.why_notable: Delayed COVID-era increases restored with an explicit below-median peer positioning claim as justification.

notable_language.quote: The Committee approved, for 2021, the original intended compensation increases from 2020. Starting January 1, 2021, his salary was $500,000 and target bonus was $1,000,000. In addition, the Committee increased Kunal’s target equity grant from $1,500,000 to $2,000,000. The Committee made these changes to improve the competitiveness of Kunal’s target total compensation. In total, Kunal’s target total compensation is below the median of the peer group.

value.why_notable: Pre-emptive framing of the year-over-year decline in reported CEO pay.

notable_language.quote: Although the 2021 Summary Compensation Table shows that Kunal’s total compensation decreased year-over-year, his 2020 compensation included a non-recurring restricted stock unit grant of $3,000,000 which will vest over five years, as disclosed in our 2021 proxy.

value.why_notable: Describes an extra equity award layered onto the bonus formula for above-target individual ratings.

notable_language.quote: In 2021, Morningstar rewarded its top performers (those whose individual performance adjustment was above 100%) with a restricted stock unit award that vests in two equal annual installments commencing on the first anniversary of the grant date.

value.why_notable: Unusually direct admission of a stock ownership compliance failure and a granted waiver.

notable_language.quote: Due to an administrative error, Gail Landis is not currently in compliance but has a plan is in place to achieve compliance no later than the second quarter of 2022. The Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee has reviewed the facts and granted Gail a waiver to the stock ownership requirements for this period of time.

value.why_notable: Uses the 97% say-on-pay result to justify making no changes.

notable_language.quote: Given the significant shareholder support, the Compensation Committee did not make any changes to the Company’s executive compensation program in response to the 2021 say on pay vote.

value.why_notable: Tightening of ownership requirements announced alongside the increase in MSU maximum payout.

notable_language.quote: Stock ownership is a cornerstone of our executive compensation program. In December 2021, we increased the holding requirement for total number of vested restricted stock units and vested market stock units from 25% to 33% for our NEOs.

investor_qa_basis.basis: management's written answers to questions submitted by investors, published roughly monthly. Same verification as every other fact — whole-document boundaries and a checked quote — but a different kind of evidence from a 10-K or proxy statement: unaudited, unprompted by any disclosure requirement, and responsive to whatever was asked. Corroborating; not a substitute for a filed disclosure.
